newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Marine sees recovery in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China Marine sees recovery in 1997.

text.p: China International Marine Containers (Group) Ltd's core container manufacturing business was expected to improve in the second quarter of 1997, group managing director Mai Bo Liang said on Wednesday.

"China's demand in containers is seen rising to 600,000 TEUs (20-foot equivalent units) in 1997 from a projected 500,000 TEUs this year while its total production capacity is due to fall due to fierce competition," Mai told a news briefing.
Oversupply had squeezed CIMC's profit margin to eight percent in the first six months of the year from an average of 12 percent a year earlier, Mai said.
The current production capacity of container makers in China totalled one million TEUs a year, two times the country's annual demand, he said.

CIMC's net profit grew 42 percent in the first half of 1996, but taking away a special 45.62 million yuan gain from the sale of its 40-percent stake in Xinhui CIMC Container Co in May, its operating profit fell more than 12 percent to 65.53 million.
Slowing Chinese exports and a 10 percent fall in container prices due to keen competition depressed earnings despite sales rising 53.10 precent in the six-month period, Mai said.
The company forecast a 30 percent growth on annual net profit for 1996, the managing director said.
Steel costs were seen continuing to fall in the second half of the year and should help offset the negative effect on sliding product prices, he said.
Supply and demand should also move toward a more balanced situation next year as a number of underperforming manufacturers were expected to be sqeezed out of the business, Mai said.
Demand was seen picking up gradually following a recovery in China's trade, after exports posted their first monthly rise of the year in July.
CIMC's Shanghai refrigerated container manufacturing project would start commercial operation later this month but Mai said he did not expect the new project to contribute to profits this year.
"We hope it can break-even but at worst it may lose HK$2 million this year," Mai said.
The CIMC group would make airport equipment and refrigerated container production its development focus next year, he added.
